uplink.description: Datalog frame: active energy import -> metering.energy.total (no per-phase register, so no channels key)
uplink._note: Upstream-example input (TTN yobiiq/em4301-ct codec yaml, Apache-2.0). expected.data via the ported upstream decoder (oracle). Sum of activeEnergyImportL123T1/T2 registers (Wh) -> metering.energy.total; the export T1/T2 registers are TARIFF BUCKETS of one meter-wide register, not physical positions, so they stay top-level camelCase extras. This frame carries no per-phase register at all, so `channels` is omitted entirely (lazy build). Satisfies power-meter via metering.energy.total.

uplink.description: Full three-phase instantaneous frame: per-phase voltage/current/active power/power factor plus the meter's own aggregates
uplink._note: In-bounds synthetic frame exercising every core per-phase register with a distinct value per phase, values taken from the register table in reference/upstream-codec.js (verified against it as oracle): voltageL1N/L2N/L3N (0x0C/0x0D/0x0E) 2301/2295/2312 x0.1 -> 230.1/229.5/231.2 V; currentL1/L2/L3 (0x10/0x11/0x12) 3500/3250/3000 mA -> 3.5/3.25/3 A; activePowerL1/L2/L3 (0x14/0x15/0x16) 800/750/700 W; powerFactorL1/L2/L3 (0x1D/0x1E/0x1F) 98/95/92 x0.01 -> 0.98/0.95/0.92. The meter's OWN whole-device aggregates stay top-level and are not repeated in any entry: activePowerL123 (0x13) 2250 W = 800+750+700, currentL123 (0x0F) 9750 mA -> 9.75 A = 3.5+3.25+3, frequency (0x23) 5000 x0.01 -> 50 Hz. Note that no top-level power.voltage exists: 0x0C is L1's own phase-to-neutral voltage, so it lives in phaseA.

uplink.description: Three-phase reactive/apparent power, phase angle and maximum current demand — per-phase extras inside the entries
uplink._note: In-bounds synthetic frame for the remaining per-phase registers, values verified against reference/upstream-codec.js as oracle: reactivePowerL1/L2/L3 (0x17/0x18/0x19) 320/300/280 x0.001 -> 0.32/0.3/0.28 kvar; apparentPowerL1/L2/L3 (0x1A/0x1B/0x1C) 816/789/761 x0.001 rounded to 2 decimals by the ported decoder -> 0.82/0.79/0.76 kVA; phaseAngleL1/L2/L3 (0x20/0x21/0x22) 1147/1810/2300 x0.01 -> 11.47/18.1/23 degrees; maximumL1/L2/L3CurrentDemand (0x27/0x28/0x29) 4200/4100/4000 mA. All four keep the vendor's value and unit verbatim as camelCase extras inside their phase's entry — only the L1/L2/L3 infix is dropped, since the entry's `channel` label carries the phase.

uplink.description: Lazy build: only L1 and L3 report, no whole-meter aggregate — power-meter is satisfied through the channels entries alone
uplink._note: In-bounds synthetic frame naming only L1 and L3 (voltageL1N/currentL1 0x0C/0x10 -> 229.8 V / 2.45 A, voltageL3N/currentL3 0x0E/0x12 -> 230.7 V / 1.98 A), verified against reference/upstream-codec.js as oracle. Exactly two entries are built and phaseB is absent because the frame carried no L2 register — not because of any sentinel value (the wire format has none, and 0 A would be a legitimate idle reading). No whole-meter register is present, so no top-level power.* key is emitted and power-meter membership resolves purely through the entries.

uplink.description: Device basic information (fPort 50): identity, class and CT/VT ratio configuration
uplink._note: Upstream-example input (TTN yobiiq/em4301-ct codec yaml, Apache-2.0). expected.data via the ported upstream decoder (oracle). Identity/config frame: no measured reading, so no `channels` key. The CT/VT ratios describe the meter's wiring configuration rather than one phase's reading, so they stay top-level extras.

uplink.description: Uplink on an fPort the meter does not use (not 0, not 1..10, not 50)
uplink._note: The ported decoder's own fPort guard (reference/upstream-codec.js `Decode`): a port outside the measurement range 1..10 and the basic-information port 50 yields the string "Incorrect fPort", which the normalization layer surfaces as a decode error instead of attaching it to a measurement. Payload bytes are the first record of the datalog frame above, to show the port alone decides.
